objective: Source control practices: Git remote/local operations, branching strategies, and semantic versioning

sources.cite: CompTIA AutoOps+ AT0-001 V1 Exam Objectives, document version 1.2: Automation Coding Concepts 31%, System Configuration 25%, Continuous Integration 24%, Continuous Delivery 20%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of CompTIA's PDF. Relevant text: 1.4 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with the code life cycle' (syntax errors, runtime errors); 2.4 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with system configuration' (syntax errors specific to configuration files); 3.2 'Explain workflow management concepts in CI' (automated rollbacks). The objective wording here is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's py-import-crash-traceback-autoopsplus (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: git revert records new commits that reverse the effect of earlier commits, leaving existing history in place; reset --hard discards work and must be used with care.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: MAJOR for incompatible API changes, MINOR for backward compatible functionality, PATCH for backward compatible fixes; a released version's contents must not be modified.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You maintain the automation repository at Granby Utilities, a fictional water utility. Twelve engineers use its modules to provision servers and network gear.
handover: main is shared and protected; releases are tagged.
The network module is at v2.3.1.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: two engineers' pushes reintroduce a3f9 and drop a teammate's commit; an afternoon goes to untangling main.
Check-in 3: overnight runs pinned to v2.3.1 fail on the renamed variable; two sites lose network provisioning.
Check-in 4: the feature branch's half-built change misconfigures a pump station's network.

undoPrompt.title: Undo a pushed commit
undoPrompt.context: a3f9 is on the shared main branch.

choices.label: git revert a3f9, push the new commit through a pull request, and tell the team

effects.log: A revert commit undoes a3f9; history stays intact.

choices.feedback: git revert records a new commit that reverses an earlier one, so others' clones stay consistent.

choices.label: Fix the playbook in a new commit on top
choices.feedback: It works if the fix is right, but takes longer while main stays broken.

choices.label: git reset --hard to the previous commit and force-push main
choices.feedback: Four engineers' clones now diverge from main; their next pushes resurrect or lose work.

choices.label: Release v3.0.0 with a changelog noting the rename and how to migrate
choices.feedback: Semantic versioning raises MAJOR for incompatible changes so callers can pin and plan.

choices.label: Release v2.4.0
choices.feedback: Callers expecting compatible changes break on upgrade.

choices.label: Move the v2.3.1 tag to the new commit
choices.feedback: A released version must not change; pinned callers get breaking code silently.

hotfixPrompt.title: A fix during feature work
hotfixPrompt.context: v3.0.0 needs a one-line fix; main has half-finished feature work.

choices.label: Branch from v3.0.0, fix, release v3.0.1, and merge the fix back into main
choices.feedback: A short-lived branch from the release isolates the fix from unfinished work, and merging back keeps main current.

choices.label: Release v3.0.1 from main
choices.feedback: The patch carries untested feature changes.

choices.label: Commit the fix to a feature branch and deploy from it
choices.feedback: Production runs unreviewed, unreleased code nobody can reproduce from a tag.

reflection.question: Write the release record for the twelve engineers.

parts.label: History and versions
parts.criteria: a3f9 reverted; v3.0.0 for the rename.
parts.modelAnswer: We reverted a3f9 with a new commit. The vlan rename is a breaking change, released as v3.0.0 with migration notes.

parts.label: Hotfix
parts.criteria: v3.0.1 from a branch off v3.0.0, merged back.
parts.modelAnswer: The urgent fix shipped as v3.0.1 from the v3.0.0 tag and is merged into main.

scoring.modelReasoning: Undo pushed commits with git revert, which records a new commit and keeps shared history intact. Version by semantic versioning: incompatible changes raise MAJOR, and a released version is never changed. Ship urgent fixes from a short-lived branch off the release and merge them back.
